{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=metrics+and+frameworks+for+autonomous+problem+selection+in+AI+research&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Agentic AI in transforming agriculture: a review. \", \"abstract\": \"Artificial intelligence-based agents are emerging as a transformative paradigm for agriculture, enabling autonomous perception, reasoning, decision-making, and coordinated action across complex data and operational environments. These systems could improve productivity, resilience, resource efficiency, and food security, while raising challenges related to robustness, interoperability, data governance, trust, equity, and regulation. This Review examines the rise of these systems in agriculture and outlines research priorities for their development and deployment.\", \"doi\": \"10.1038/s44264-026-00199-w\", \"pmid\": \"42996690\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13739721\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1038/s44264-026-00199-w\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13739721\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13739721?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"The more you automate, the less you see: Hidden pitfalls of autonomous AI scientists.\", \"abstract\": \"The rapid rise of autonomous AI scientists marks a paradigm shift in scientific discovery by automating the research lifecycle. Yet their rushed development has outpaced critical oversight, leaving key workflow decisions dangerously unscrutinized. We present a much-needed systematic analysis of open-source AI scientist systems, investigating four primary pitfalls: inappropriate benchmark selection, data leakage, metric misuse, and post hoc selection bias. Through controlled experiments that isolate each pitfall, we find systematic vulnerabilities across two representative open-source systems. Crucially, we find that these flaws are largely invisible at the level of the final manuscript, suggesting that current manuscript-centric peer review paradigms are fundamentally insufficient for ensuring the integrity of automated research. We further propose mitigation strategies and demonstrate that access to full workflow artifacts (log traces and code) enables more effective auditing. Our findings suggest that journals, conferences, and researchers should move beyond manuscript-only evaluation toward process auditing the end-to-end workflow artifacts of AI scientist systems.\", \"doi\": \"10.1073/pnas.2610214123\", \"pmid\": \"42832657\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13663820\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2610214123\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13663820\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13663820?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.\", \"abstract\": \"

Introduction

Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation.

Methods

A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations.

Results

Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance.

Discussion

AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fcvm.2026.1966224\", \"pmid\": \"42991531\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13736032\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1966224\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13736032\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13736032?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges.\", \"abstract\": \"Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability.
